A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Better Embeddings with Coupled Adam. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated figures and renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, embedding measurements, optimizer ablations, and empirical fits in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds individual downstream-task results in Appendix G.3, Tables 8–11.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (24) retain the same vocabulary-wise averaging of embedding second moments. Embedding-only coupling, standard Adam for other parameters, and the optimizer procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebText and SlimPajama, the same seven downstream tasks, and the same four word-similarity benchmarks. Tables 8–11 disclose results for tasks already evaluated in v1; they add no datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Standard Adam and momentum SGD remain the evaluated comparators in their corresponding experiments. The added citation to Rudman and Eickhoff (2024) is related-work discussion, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The training grids, budgets, architectures, metrics, and hyperparameter searches are retained. Table 6 changes the labels 124M/350M to 125M/355M, matching the grid already stated in v1 Section 4.1; unchanged layer counts, widths, heads, and learning rates support treating this as a documentation correction.

E4.justification: The scaling-exponent sweep and SGD learning-rate search test the same questions with the same settings. New Tables 10–11 disaggregate their existing downstream evaluations by task, without introducing a new ablation, robustness test, or explanatory analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds for small-scale experiments and ablations, one run for large-scale experiments, and the same one-sided 95% Student's t-test in Appendix F. Added tables reuse existing reporting conventions. Changed plotted uncertainty-bar magnitudes are result changes, with no documented revision to the estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 8–11 substantially expand result reporting with seven-task breakdowns across the main experiments and both ablations. For example, at 210B tokens/2.6B parameters, new Table 9 reports Coupled/standard accuracies of 0.32/0.29 on ARC challenge and 0.61/0.63 on LAMBADA, behind unchanged averages of 0.492/0.490. Existing table values are retained, but ablation uncertainty bars are approximately halved in v3 Figure 3 versus v1 Figure 2, and in Figure 8.

T1.justification: The gradient and mean-shift derivations, mathematical assumptions, and Appendix D lemma, theorem, and proofs are retained. Figure 1's corrected update-vector terminology aligns its caption with existing Equations (11) and (16), without revising the formal argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: Adam's second moments contribute to anisotropy, coupling improves embeddings, and upstream/downstream benefits depend on sufficiently large training datasets.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly states that fine-tuning tasks were not tested and identifies extension beyond SGD and Adam as future work. Existing interpretations concerning dataset size, batch size, and residual shifts from weight tying remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 6 corrects model-size labels to agree with the documented experimental grid, and Section 9 explicitly describes downstream evaluation as few-shot. Hyperparameters, compute disclosures, implementation descriptions, and the code-access statement otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds Rudman and Eickhoff (2024), Stable Anisotropic Regularization, and briefly discusses IsoScore-based regularization for fine-tuning. The remaining citations and positioning relative to earlier optimizer and anisotropy research are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section structure remain unchanged. Local edits correct terminology and typos, expand related work and limitations, update cross-references, and reorganize Appendix G around the relocated plot and new task-level results.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 7 moves from the appendix to become v3 Figure 2, and four task-level tables are added. Figures are redrawn with revised legends and some axis ranges; Figure 1 replaces gradient labels with update-vector labels. The overall document and table formats remain similar.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–11 improve transparency by exposing task-level trade-offs hidden by v1's averages. Corrected Figure 1 terminology and the explicit fine-tuning limitation also improve clarity. These are useful but limited gains in an otherwise unchanged study; the unexplained reduction of ablation uncertainty bars remains a reporting ambiguity.
